schema: CUDA-core (scan.cu) route falsification: 2-D-over-d_state warp-split forward premise falsified on B200.
provenance: box session record 2026-06-26; the bench script printed to stdout and the log was not retained
remeasure: box burst 1 — rerun scratch/cuda_inc2_forward_bench.py with a JSON writer (add --out flag)

result.relative_speed_vs_official_forward: ~0.18x (approx 5.6x slower than official mamba_ssm selective_scan_fn forward at both bench shapes)
result.conclusion: Both naive CUDA kernels measured approximately 5.6x slower than the official mamba_ssm selective_scan_fn forward at the N=128 bench shapes. The 2-D warp-split approach did not yield a speedup over the serial kernel at these shapes.

structural_reason: The naive kernels lack the two structural advantages of the official kernel: (a) d-major [B, D, L] memory layout (our kernels use [B, L, D] which is L-major, causing non-coalesced d_state access at large D), and (b) kNItems time-tiling (the official kernel tiles L in registers, amortizing global memory traffic per thread). These are the real levers for competitive scan performance at large D and N.

kernels.name: forward_scan
kernels.description: SISO selective scan forward using cub::BlockScan; [B,L,D] layout, serial d_state

kernels.name: forward_scan_2d
kernels.description: SISO forward, 2-D warp-split over d_state (warps=4/8/16/32); N<=128; statically-allocated y_red buffer

kernels.name: forward_scan_tiled
kernels.description: SISO forward, d-major [B,D,L] layout + kNItems time-tiling (the official kernel structure); N<=128

kernels.name: backward_scan
kernels.description: SISO selective scan backward, d-major layout; not benchmarked in inc2 forward bench

disposition: scan.cu retained as an explicit archived negative. The falsification of the 2-D-over-d_state forward premise motivated the pivot to the tcgen05/cutlass-DSL GDN-2 native backward approach.
what_was_not_tested: forward_scan_tiled (kNItems tiling, d-major) was not included in the BENCH_SHAPES comparison against the official forward at the time of the negative result. It represents the closer approximation to the official structure and should be included in any re-measurement.
